text: Thornbury's board includes external members with no Tableau license and no access to the internal network. Tableau Public exists for exactly this situation: a browser link anyone can open, no login required.

But Tableau Public can't maintain a live connection to a private, on-premises SQL Server database. Publishing requires converting the data source to an extract first — a saved snapshot of the exact same correct warehouse data.

That doesn't compromise correctness. The extract is the same real numbers, taken at one point in time — what's lost is automatic refresh, not accuracy. Keeping it current just means refreshing the extract and republishing before each QBR cycle.
With the Board's deck published, next chapter builds the third and final front-end, completely independently: Finance's own Excel reconciliation workbook.
